about: Singers' voices as measured, for holding VocalWind's to them (voice-range.mjs, the range check: the owner, 15 November 2026, of the singing dynamics design's fourth item, "Yes, as designed"). Each measurement with its source; the papers in the trunk's research-downloads/voice/ (its README). Levels in dB SPL at 30 cm.

threshold.about: The phonation threshold pressure by pitch, Pth = kpa[0] + kpa[1] (F0 / f0_mean_hz)^2 kPa, f0_mean_hz the speakers' mean speaking pitch; and the least pressure trained singers sang at, over it (the tenors' softest notes 50 to 100% above their threshold, the non-singers' none below 100%). Measured to some 400 Hz (the tenors' 383 Hz; the women at their speaking pitch): above it, a reach.
threshold.source: I. R. Titze & J. Sundberg 1992, "Vocal intensity in speakers and singers", JASA 91(5), 2936-2946, doi:10.1121/1.402929: eq. (37) and its text (in its authors' NCVS Status and Progress Report 2, April 1992, 17-37)

sulter1995.about: Voice range profiles on /a/, dB(A) at 30 cm, an FST-II phonetometer: each group's mean pitch (Hz) and its least and greatest SPL at each tenth of its members' ranges, 0 to 100%, with their standard deviations (Tables 1-3). Trained: two years' lessons or choir at the least. Above some 70% of a man's range and 50-60% of a woman's, falsetto (mechanism 2).
sulter1995.source: A. M. Sulter, H. K. Schutte & D. G. Miller 1995, "Differences in phonetogram features between male and female subjects with and without vocal training", J Voice 9(4), 363-377, doi:10.1016/S0892-1997(05)80198-5 (as chapter 8 of Sulter's 1996 Groningen thesis)

lamarche2010.about: Thirty female opera soloists' voice range profiles at 30 cm (Table 4), the physiological task (the voice's whole range, as loud and as soft as it goes: 8 sopranos, 2 mezzos, 6 contraltos) and the performance tasks' discrete pitches (16, 8 and 6): each category's mean, with the sopranos' standard deviation. spl_extent: a pitch's height from its least to its greatest SPL, the mean over the range; spl_range: the greatest less the least anywhere.
lamarche2010.source: A. Lamarche, S. Ternström & P. Pabon 2010, "The Singer's Voice Range Profile: Female Professional Opera Soloists", J Voice 24(4), 410-426, doi:10.1016/j.jvoice.2008.12.008 (as Paper I of Lamarche's 2009 KTH thesis, "Putting the Singing Voice on the Map")

monson2012.source: B. Monson, A. Lotto & B. Story 2012, "Analysis of high-frequency energy in long-term average spectra of singing, speech, and voiceless fricatives", JASA 132(3), 1754-1764, doi:10.1121/1.4742724 (PMC3460988; research-downloads/voice/monson-lotto-story-2012-hfe), Table IV
monson2012.method: Fifteen trained singers, eight of them women, singing phrases in their normal performance voice, recorded anechoically to 20 kHz: each third-octave band's mean level, dB SPL at 1 m, by sex, singing and speaking. Read by vtl-fit spectra (src/bin/vtl-fit.rs), each band against its own overall level, beside a sung stem's.
